title: China Shipping: Asia-Europe Rates Rise and US Port Risks
metaDescription: Asia-Europe spot rates climb as FAK hikes loom. US lawmakers push for more Cosco ship inspections amid espionage claims. Port congestion eases.
bottomLine: Asia-Europe spot rates rose 6% to 7% this week, ending a three-month decline. US political pressure on Cosco could lead to slower port processing for their vessels.

stories.headline: Asia-Europe spot rates climb ahead of October FAK hikes
stories.tldr: Shanghai to Rotterdam spot rates rose 6% to $3,522 per 40ft this week, ending a three-month downward trend.
stories.whatHappened:
The World Container Index from Drewry shows a price reversal on Asia-Europe trades. The Shanghai-Rotterdam leg increased 6% to $3,522 per 40ft in the week ending 16 October. 

The Shanghai-Genoa route rose 7% to $3,945 per 40ft. These increases come as carriers prepare and implement new Freight All Kinds (FAK) price hikes this month to counteract the previous three months of declining spot rates.
stories.whyItMatters:
You cannot rely on the sliding scale of the last quarter to lower your landed costs. If you are booking spot for Q4 stock, the window for the lowest prices has closed. You are now paying a premium for the same space you could have secured cheaper a fortnight ago.

For sellers with tight margins on bulky goods, a 6% to 7% jump in ocean freight eats directly into your net profit. You need to check if your forwarder is passing through these FAK hikes now or delaying them until your cargo hits the water, as this affects your cash flow forecasting for November.
stories.hotTake: Carriers are testing the water to see if you will pay more before the peak season rush. I would lock in a short-term contract now if you have volume, because these 'corrections' usually lead to steeper climbs. Do not bet on a return to September pricing.
actions: Compare your current spot quotes against the $3,522 benchmark for Rotterdam.
Ask your forwarder for the specific FAK hike schedule for the remainder of October.

stories.headline: US lawmakers push for increased Cosco ship inspections
stories.tldr: Three US House committee chairs want the Coast Guard to revoke special inspection privileges for Cosco vessels over espionage claims.
stories.whatHappened:
House Republicans John Moolenaar, Rick Crawford, and Carlos Gimenez wrote to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on 14 October. They requested the removal of Cosco vessels from the Qualship 21 program, which currently allows ships with strong safety records to undergo fewer routine port state control inspections.

The lawmakers cite a Reuters report alleging Cosco uses concealed equipment to intercept military communications near US coastlines. The letter identifies 11 vessels, including COSCO DEVELOPMENT, COSCO PRIDE and COSCO VIETNAM. Cosco and the Chinese embassy deny these claims, stating equipment is for commercial navigation.
stories.whyItMatters:
If the US Coast Guard increases inspections, Cosco ships will spend more time sitting at anchor or in berth. This adds unpredictable dwell time to your US inbound shipments. An intensive inspection is not a quick check; it is a process that can delay a vessel by several hours or days.

If you use Cosco for your primary lanes, you face a higher risk of schedule slips. A ship that is flagged for an intensive inspection does not leave the port on time, and that delay cascades through your entire FBA inbound plan, potentially missing your receiving windows.
stories.hotTake: This is political theatre that creates real operational friction. I do not care about the espionage claims, but I care about my containers sitting in a harbor for an extra three days. Diversify your carrier mix now to avoid being caught in a single-carrier bottleneck.
actions: Audit your current shipments to see how many are on Cosco vessels.
Build a three-day buffer into your US warehouse receiving dates for Cosco bookings.

stories.headline: Asian port congestion eases but Shanghai hotspots remain
stories.tldr: General port bottlenecks in Asia are easing due to holiday-related cargo reductions, though some Shanghai terminals still face berthing delays.
stories.whatHappened:
Freight forwarders report a general easing of bottlenecks across key Asian ports. This improvement follows a reduction in cargo volumes related to holidays, which has reduced the pressure on terminal operations and equipment availability.

Despite the overall trend, specific terminal hotspots persist. Forwarders note that berthing delays are still present within individual terminals in Shanghai. This means that while the port of Shanghai as a whole looks better on paper, your specific cargo may still face delays depending on which terminal it is assigned to.
stories.whyItMatters:
You can breathe easier on your general lead times, but you cannot assume a clear run through Shanghai. If your factory is in the Yangtze River Delta, your goods might still get stuck at the terminal gate while other parts of the port are flowing smoothly.

For those shipping urgent Q4 stock, do not let a 'congestion is easing' headline trick you into cutting your lead time buffers. The 'hotspots' are where your specific container will likely end up if you are using the largest terminals. A three-day delay at the berth is still a three-day delay for your customer.
stories.hotTake: General easing is a lie for the operator. Until every terminal in Shanghai is clear, you are still at the mercy of the terminal operator's schedule. Keep your buffers and do not trust the macro data when your cargo is in a specific micro-location.
actions: Check with your forwarder which specific Shanghai terminals are currently experiencing berthing delays.
Maintain your current lead time buffers despite reports of easing congestion.

stories.headline: Carriers shift green transition costs to price-sensitive shippers
stories.tldr: Shipping lines claim they are bearing the cost of alternative fuels and lower-emission vessels as shippers resist paying green premiums.
stories.whatHappened:
Speakers at the Singapore International Bunkering Conference and Exhibition stated that carriers are shouldering the financial burden of the green transition. They are investing in alternative fuels and lower-emission vessels to meet environmental goals.

Chia Yujin, head of operations and procurement (China) for Pacific International Lines (PIL), noted that shippers in price-sensitive markets are not yet ready to pay the additional costs associated with the industry's transition to greener shipping methods.
stories.whyItMatters:
You are currently benefiting from carriers absorbing these costs, but this is a temporary state. As carriers face mounting pressure to decarbonise, they will eventually force these costs onto the shipper through new surcharges or higher base rates.

If you market your products as 'sustainable' or 'green', you are now in a position to negotiate these costs or find carriers who offer certified green lanes. However, for the bulk of ecommerce operators, this means a new category of 'green fees' is likely to appear in your quotes within the next 12 to 24 months.
stories.hotTake: The 'green transition' is just the next excuse for a GRI. Carriers will claim they are saving the planet while they raise your rates by 10%. Start budgeting for a 'carbon surcharge' now so it does not shock your P&L next year.
actions: Review your current carrier contracts for any mentions of upcoming environmental surcharges.
Ask your forwarder if they have access to lower-emission vessels and what the price premium is.

contentHooks: Spot rates on the Shanghai-Rotterdam lane just jumped 6% and the slide is over.
Political fights over Cosco espionage could mean your containers sit longer in US ports.
Do not trust the 'congestion is easing' reports if your goods are moving through Shanghai.
Carrier FAK hikes in October are ending the era of cheap Asia-Europe shipping.
Qualship 21 privileges for Cosco are under fire, and that means more inspections.
Your landed cost just went up 7% on the Shanghai-Genoa route this week.
The gap between 'general port easing' and 'terminal hotspots' is where your profit disappears.
Diversifying carriers is no longer about price, it is about avoiding political inspection bottlenecks.
October is the month the Asia-Europe freight market stopped falling.
Check your Cosco bookings before the US Coast Guard starts slowing them down.

faq.question: Are shipping rates from China to Europe going up again?
faq.answer: Yes. Spot rates rose this week, ending a three-month decline. The Shanghai-Rotterdam route increased 6% to $3,522 per 40ft, and Shanghai-Genoa rose 7% to $3,945 per 40ft due to October FAK hikes.

faq.question: Will Cosco shipments face delays at US ports?
faq.answer: There is a high risk. US lawmakers are pushing the Coast Guard to remove Cosco from the Qualship 21 program, which would increase the frequency and depth of inspections for their vessels.

faq.question: Is port congestion in China currently a problem?
faq.answer: It is improving overall, but specific hotspots remain. While general bottlenecks are easing, some terminals in Shanghai still experience berthing delays that can affect your departure schedules.
